title: Finite reduction preserves the canonical adjoint mates
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $B=A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On their small pro-etale sites use $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, and $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use pullback, compact supports, tensor, and exceptional adjunctions as in [def-pur-co-smoothness, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], their canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction, lem-coef-finite-exceptional], and the projection map of [def-exchange-projection].

For a smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, put $\omega_{f,A}=Rf_A^!A_Y$ and let $\theta_{f,A,K}:Lf_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to Rf_A^!K$ be the canonical tensor map specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Under the pullback, tensor and exceptional coefficient comparisons,
$$Q_X(\theta_{f,A,K})=\theta_{f,B,Q_YK}.$$
For composable smooth separated maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions, the canonical exceptional composition comparison $c_{g,f,A}:R(gf)_A^!\xrightarrow\sim Rf_A^!Rg_A^!$ is also identified by reduction with $c_{g,f,B}$. For a Cartesian square with this $f$, arbitrary $v:Y'\to Y$, and projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, reduction identifies the canonical extraordinary comparison $\beta_{f,v,A,K}:Lu^*Rf_A^!K\to Rf_A'^!Lv^*K$ with $\beta_{f,v,B,Q_YK}$; at $K=A_Y$ these are the coefficient-object comparisons of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Finally, for any separated finite-type $h:T\to U$, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ and $a:Rh_{!,A}M\to L$, reduction identifies the adjoint transpose $Rh_A^!(a)\circ\eta_{A,M}$ with the transpose of the reduced $a$, under the compact-support and exceptional coefficient comparisons.

source.place: Proof Step 2: coefficient compatibility of the tensor formula and exceptional-adjunction composition; agent-written extraction of the returned split Step 2

proof.text:
Write $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}$, $G_{h,R}=Rh_R^!$ for $R=A,B$. Let $q_{h,M}:Q_UF_{h,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,B}Q_TM$ and $b_{h,L}:Q_TG_{h,A}L\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,B}Q_UL$ for $h:T\to U$. The finite-Tor clause of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] supplies the pullback and tensor comparisons. The unconditional finite constructible theorem [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] supplies $b$, with precisely the same $q$ as the compact-support coefficient comparison. In our indices its two normalization equations are
$$G_{h,B}(q_{h,M})b_{h,F_{h,A}M}Q_T(\eta_{A,M})=\eta_{B,Q_TM},$$
$$\epsilon_{B,Q_UL}F_{h,B}(b_{h,L})q_{h,G_{h,A}L}=Q_U(\epsilon_{A,L}).$$
All schemes and coefficient rings here satisfy that theorem's hypotheses: separated finite type over the fixed algebraic closure, $A=A_{E,n}$, $B=A_{E,m}$ and $n\ge m\ge1$. In particular we do not invoke the conditional exceptional-admissibility clause of the operation-reduction node. All subsequent calculations take place on its finite constructible finite-Tor domains.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text:
First prove the last clause, for the arbitrary $h$ in the statement. Put $a_B=Q_U(a)q_{h,M}^{-1}:F_{h,B}Q_TM\to Q_UL$. Naturality of $b$ at $a:F_{h,A}M\to L$ and then the unit identity of Step 1 give
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{h,L}Q_T(G_{h,A}(a)\eta_{A,M})
&=G_{h,B}(Q_Ua)b_{h,F_{h,A}M}Q_T\eta_{A,M}\\
&=G_{h,B}(Q_Ua)G_{h,B}(q_{h,M}^{-1})\eta_{B,Q_TM}\\
&=G_{h,B}(a_B)\eta_{B,Q_TM}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required equality of transposes. The formula $a^\sharp=G(a)\eta$ is the ordinary adjunction formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] (specialize the square to a morphism). Thus the assertion is an explicit three-line substitution into the cited unit identity, and will also be applied to the two particular counit composites below.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text:
The projection transformation itself reduces. Denote by $P_R(M,K):F_{f,R}M\otimes_R^LK\to F_{f,R}(M\otimes_R^Lf_R^*K)$ the map of [def-exchange-projection]. Its formula at a compactification is the proper counit-defined projection map followed by the canonical open tensor comparison. The comparison $q$ of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] is compatible with pullback and the counits defining this projection transformation; [lem-fix-operation-reduction] additionally identifies its tensor associators and adjunction structure maps. Substituting those identified arrows in the displayed definition gives, under the tensor/pullback comparisons,
$$q_{f,M\otimes f_A^*K}\,Q_Y(P_A(M,K))=P_B(Q_XM,Q_YK)\,(q_{f,M}\otimes1).$$
Here $M=\omega_{f,A}=G_{f,A}A_Y$ is a permitted finite-Tor constructible input by the functors in [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. The invertibility of $P_A(\omega_{f,A},K)$ and its $B$ counterpart is exactly [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], including its pro-etale realization clause. Taking inverses in the displayed square is legitimate: a functor sends an inverse to an inverse, by applying it to the two inverse identities.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text: Let $t_{R,K}:F_{f,R}(f_R^*K\otimes_R^L\omega_{f,R})\to K$ be the composite in clause 2 of [def-pur-co-smoothness]: apply tensor symmetry, $P_R(\omega_{f,R},K)^{-1}$, then $\epsilon_{R,R_Y}\otimes1$ and the tensor unitor. The map $\theta_{f,R,K}$ is its adjoint transpose. Identify $Q_X\omega_{f,A}$ with $\omega_{f,B}$ by $b_{f,A_Y}$ and $Q_YA_Y=B_Y$. The inverse-projection square of Step 3 identifies the middle arrow of $Q_Yt_{A,K}$ with the corresponding $B$ arrow. The counit equation of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identifies the next arrow. Symmetry and the unitor are the canonical tensor comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] (equivalently swap the two factors in the reassociated derived tensor). Hence $Q_Yt_{A,K}$, conjugated by $q$ and these source identifications, is exactly $t_{B,Q_YK}$. Apply Step 2 with $M=f_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}$ and $a=t_{A,K}$. This yields $b_{f,K}Q_X\theta_{f,A,K}=\theta_{f,B,Q_YK}$ under the stated source identifications, as required.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text:
For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ write $\alpha_R:F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf,R}$ for compact-support composition. The canonical $c_R:G_{gf,R}\to G_{f,R}G_{g,R}$ is its adjunction conjugate: $c_{R,L}$ is the transpose of $\epsilon_{gf,R,L}\alpha_{R,G_{gf,R}L}$ under $F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\dashv G_{f,R}G_{g,R}$. The composite counit is $\epsilon_{g,R}\circ F_{g,R}(\epsilon_{f,R}G_{g,R})$, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The precise left-hand comparison equation is supplied by [lem-sf-compact-coefficient-composition]:
$$q_{gf}Q_Z\alpha_A=\alpha_B(F_{g,B}q_f)(q_gF_{f,A}).$$
Take mates of this equation. The right mate of each coefficient square $q_h^{-1}$ is $b_h$, by the counit equation of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] says that the mate for the composite adjunction is
$$b_{\mathrm{comp},L}=G_{f,B}(b_{g,L})\,b_{f,G_{g,A}L}.$$
Clause 3 of the same node says that replacing the left adjunction by $\alpha_R$ replaces the mate by its conjugate $c_R$. Therefore the mates of the two equal pasted squares give the explicit equation
$$b_{\mathrm{comp},L}\,Q_X(c_{A,L})=c_{B,Q_ZL}\,b_{gf,L}.$$
This is exactly the claimed reduction compatibility for $c$, with all domains and directions specified. Only the existing general mate-pasting theorem and the compact-support composition square are used; no purity orientation is involved.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text:
For the Cartesian square write $E_{R,M}:v_R^*F_{f,R}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f',R}u_R^*M$ for compact-support exchange. Its defining compactification formula [def-exchange-projection] is proper direct-image exchange followed by open-extension base change; direct-image exchange is the displayed unit--square-comparison--counit composite. The finite-reduction structural compatibility of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], together with the pullback compatibility of the compact-support comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], identifies these arrows. Explicitly, after the pullback identifications, their equality is
$$q_{f',u_A^*M}\,Q_{Y'}(E_{A,M})=E_{B,Q_XM}\,v_B^*(q_{f,M}).$$
This follows by replacing the three factors in the direct-image exchange formula by their reduced factors, and then replacing the open tensor/base-change identification by its coefficient identification; both resulting composites are the compactification exchange formula over $B$. The direct-image comparison used in that formula is only for the proper compactification factor (hence compact support), not an assertion for arbitrary finite-level ordinary direct images. For every input used below, $M$ is bounded constructible and has an etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Thus [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] makes both $E$ maps isomorphisms for arbitrary $v$, so the same square identifies their inverses.

source.place: Step 2, coefficient compatibility of the specified operation maps

proof.text:
The canonical extraordinary comparison at an arbitrary $K$ is the $F_{f',R}\dashv G_{f',R}$ transpose of
$$s_{R,K}=v_R^*(\epsilon_{f,R,K})\,E_{R,G_{f,R}K}^{-1}:F_{f',R}u_R^*G_{f,R}K\longrightarrow v_R^*K.$$
This is the inverse-exchange counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; at $K=R_Y$ it is exactly the displayed coefficient-object definition in clause 3 of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. By Step 6, reduction identifies the inverse exchange in $s_A$ with that in $s_B$. By the counit identity of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], it identifies the remaining factor with $v_B^*\epsilon_{f,B,Q_YK}$, using $u_B^*b_{f,K}$ to compare the source objects. Consequently $Q_{Y'}s_{A,K}$, after $q_{f'}$ and the pullback comparisons, is precisely $s_{B,Q_YK}$. Applying the explicit transpose identity of Step 2 to $h=f'$ gives
$$b_{f',v_A^*K}\,Q_{X'}(\beta_{f,v,A,K})=\beta_{f,v,B,Q_YK}\,u_B^*(b_{f,K}),$$
where $Q_{X'}u_A^*=u_B^*Q_X$ and $Q_{Y'}v_A^*=v_B^*Q_Y$ are understood. Setting $K=A_Y$ gives the coefficient-object comparisons because $Q_YA_Y=B_Y$, proving the remaining clause.
